headline: Police cannot carry out crossfire even if government orders it: Adviser Zahed
summary: Prime Minister’s Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman clarified that police officers are not obliged to obey unlawful instructions, responding to recent remarks by the IGP.
details: Prime Minister’s Adviser on Information and Cultural Affairs Zahed Ur Rahman stated that the government cannot order police to perform 'crossfire' and officers cannot execute such orders as they are not obliged to obey unlawful instructions.
The remarks come after Inspector General of Police (IGP) Md Ali Hossain Fakir recently suggested that police would resort to crossfire if necessary and permitted by the government.
Adviser Zahed noted that the IGP has since acknowledged the problematic nature of his statement and has stepped back from his original position.
The adviser further mentioned that the prime minister is currently abroad in Japan and will consider the government's final position on the matter upon his return.
When asked if an explanation was sufficient to absolve the IGP of responsibility, Zahed replied that he believed it could be, given the IGP had retracted his position.
In other news, Zahed stated that ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina would have to face justice if she returns to Bangladesh, though she would not face mob violence.
The government is also taking the rise of fundamentalism and far-right movements seriously, with strict measures being taken in response to incidents like the killing of a person in Satkhira.
Zahed added that some incidents have been prevented through prior intelligence, though these interventions are often not visible to the public.
caption:
Can the police carry out 'crossfire' if ordered? Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman says no—unlawful instructions must not be obeyed.

Prime Minister’s Adviser on Information and Cultural Affairs Zahed Ur Rahman stated that the government cannot order police to perform 'crossfire' and officers cannot execute such orders as they are not obliged to obey unlawful instructions.

The remarks come after Inspector General of Police (IGP) Md Ali Hossain Fakir recently suggested that police would resort to crossfire if necessary and permitted by the government.

Adviser Zahed noted that the IGP has since acknowledged the problematic nature of his statement and has stepped back from his original position.

The adviser further mentioned that the prime minister is currently abroad in Japan and will consider the government's final position on the matter upon his return.

When asked if an explanation was sufficient to absolve the IGP of responsibility, Zahed replied that he believed it could be, given the IGP had retracted his position.

In other news, Zahed stated that ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina would have to face justice if she returns to Bangladesh, though she would not face mob violence.

The government is also taking the rise of fundamentalism and far-right movements seriously, with strict measures being taken in response to incidents like the killing of a person in Satkhira.

Zahed added that some incidents have been prevented through prior intelligence, though these interventions are often not visible to the public.

headline_marked: [[Coal-laden cargo vessel sinks]] in Pasur river near Mongla port after collision
headline: Coal-laden cargo vessel sinks in Pasur river near Mongla port after collision
summary: A cargo vessel carrying 1,200 tonnes of coal sank in the Pasur river early today after being struck by an oil tanker. The nine crew members aboard managed to swim to safety.
details: A cargo vessel, MV Fulbari, reportedly carrying 1,200 tonnes of coal, sank in the Pasur river near Mongla port early today. The incident occurred after the vessel was hit by an oil tanker, MT Jannatul Ferdous.
The nine crew members aboard MV Fulbari managed to swim to a nearby cargo ship and took shelter there. No casualties were reported from the sinking.

According to crew members, MV Fulbari was transporting coal from MV Yas Jupiter, a foreign commercial vessel anchored at Hiron Point in Mongla port, and was heading towards Dhaka when the accident happened.

Commodore Md Shafiqul Islam Sarker, member (harbour and marine) of Mongla Port Authority, confirmed the sinking. He stated that vessel movement through the Pasur channel is continuing as normal and that the vessel's owners are taking steps to salvage the sunken ship.
The sunken vessel is owned by IRS International and was scheduled to transport the coal to Badamtala in Dhaka.
caption:
A coal-laden cargo vessel has sunk in the Pasur river near Mongla port after a collision with an oil tanker. All nine crew members were rescued.

A cargo vessel, MV Fulbari, reportedly carrying 1,200 tonnes of coal, sank in the Pasur river near Mongla port early today. The incident occurred after the vessel was hit by an oil tanker, MT Jannatul Ferdous.

The nine crew members aboard MV Fulbari managed to swim to a nearby cargo ship and took shelter there. No casualties were reported from the sinking.

According to crew members, MV Fulbari was transporting coal from MV Yas Jupiter, a foreign commercial vessel anchored at Hiron Point in Mongla port, and was heading towards Dhaka when the accident happened.

Commodore Md Shafiqul Islam Sarker, member (harbour and marine) of Mongla Port Authority, confirmed the sinking. He stated that vessel movement through the Pasur channel is continuing as normal and that the vessel's owners are taking steps to salvage the sunken ship.

The sunken vessel is owned by IRS International and was scheduled to transport the coal to Badamtala in Dhaka.
